text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Moslem community rejected reports that it had funded the oppositon Zambia Democratic Congress in its election campaign last year and was now pressing for President Frederick Chiluba to be toppled.
- Over 1,000 municipal employees have gone on strike to push for the payment of salary arrears.
- The municipality in the mining town of Kitwe has joined Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines to form resettlement committees which will explain to 10,000 squatters why they have to move from ZCCM land.
- Six armed bandits have raided a Lusaka police post, killing one policeman.
- The son of deputy chief justice Bonaventure Bwepue has been jailed for 15 years for robbery with aggravating circumstances.
- The United States has pledged financial support for Zambia's anti-AIDS drive.
